strings.SLU_Two_Faces_Labour_desc:
Saint Lucia's political habitat is ruled by a Janus-faced diarchy that remains nominally united under the Labour banner. In recent years, as anticolonial sentiment has become especially alluring to the left-wing party's populist segments, a Black Power wing has inevitably split from the original, unionist strand, effectively creating an equal-chanced factionalism within the SLLP.

This ideological struggle within the party ignites a powder keg on the island where they reign undisputedly while bickering amongst themselves — any conflict they may have will most certainly wreak havoc on the fragile balance keeping Saint Lucia's worst excesses in check.
strings.SLU_Ruins_Metayage_desc:
During its agrarian days, Saint Lucia had managed to avoid becoming a full plantation economy by adapting a form of sharecropping known nowadays as métayage, which, despite its more egalitarian outlook, had also resulted in severe economic stagnation. Moreover, it had created a stark divide between the prevalently forward-looking city dwellers and the general peasantry.

Since the 1950s, in an attempt to proletarianize the rural banana farmers and to encourage land development, the system had been officially abolished by Castries, with non-compliance often being met with harsh enforcement. As a consequence, even after more than a decade, the transition remains unpopular with the countryside despite its undeniable economic fruits.
